defect.summary: Two of the twenty frozen verdict scenarios have been failing in every sweep since T8 shipped, and the differential could never report it because the failure is a CONSTANT. `sig/f3-consistent-report` reads CANNOT_ASSESS where the baseline says SILENT; `sig/f3-contradiction-f1-silent` reads CANNOT_ASSESS where the baseline says ALARM with SIG_F3_DECLARED_VS_CLERK_CLOCK_CONTRADICTION. Both with the same live detail: 'CHAIN_IDENTITY_MISSING: 2 stamp(s) carry NO chainIdentity and 0 carry one this run could not check. ALL OF THEM ARE REFUSED and none is joined.' The suite has read 26 passed, 2 failed since, on a file the core door pins and reports as CLOSED.
defect.ground: THE BASELINE WAS NEVER WRONG - THE FIXTURE WAS, AND I HAD IT THE OTHER WAY ROUND FIRST. My first diagnosis (board, 12:0xZ) said two frozen scenarios 'still record the world T8 abolished'. Measured further: F3_SOURCE in verdict-logic.test.ts builds its clerk stamps with NO chainIdentity field at all, so T8 - ticket T8-chain-identity-mandatory, installed, re-pinned and SPENT - refuses them wholesale and F3 goes blind. The frozen entries record the readings T8 PRESERVED. Repairing the fixture restores them and the frozen file needs NO EDIT to either one: measured, 11 lines added and 0 removed, all 20 existing entries byte-identical, exactly one added. AND THE SHAPE OF THE REPAIR IS T6's, ONE TICKET EARLIER, WRITTEN INTO THE FILE THIS TICKET OPENS. F3_SOURCE's own comment reads: 'Until T6 the join ignored this field, so these fixtures could name any writer and still join. Under T6 a disagreeing stamp is DISCARDED and DISCLOSED, so a fixture modelling an ORDINARY carry must agree. The DELIBERATE mismatch now has its own scenario rather than being every fixture's incidental state.' That is this case one ticket earlier and it settles the design question without my having to choose: the ordinary carry is updated to satisfy the new precondition, and the deliberate violation gets its own scenario. Re-freezing the two entries to the blind reading was the alternative and it would have been wrong twice over - it would record a fixture accident as the expected behaviour of the sensor, and it would delete two of the three F3 exercises in the frozen set. COST TODAY IS ZERO ON THE LIVE RECORD: decision 615 reads MICA/Sig SILENT, because the live stamps carry chain identity where these fixtures did not; this is a fixture-era fact and not a deployment one, checked before it was written down.

arbiter.word: I, the arbiter, grant T25: the F3 freeze specimens name the chain their stamps belong to, as T8 requires of every stamp, and the stamps that name none become a scenario of their own; a rule worth shipping is worth a specimen, and a baseline is not re-written to match an accident.

conditions: 1. F3_SOURCE's two stamp literals gain `chainIdentity`, and the two configs that inject that source gain `expectedChainIdentity`. Four lines of fixture, no change to any reader.

2. NO READER, NO RULE AND NO BASELINE ENTRY IS EDITED. The two existing frozen readings are restored by the fixture repair, not rewritten: measured, `git diff --numstat` on verdict-logic.frozen.json is 11 insertions and 0 DELETIONS, all 20 pre-existing entries byte-identical, exactly one added. If a reviewer finds an edited baseline entry, this condition is broken and the ticket is not what it says.

3. THE DELIBERATE VIOLATION BECOMES ITS OWN SCENARIO, as T6 did for the writer mismatch: `sig/f3-no-chain-identity` uses the SAME specs and the SAME reversed clerk order as the contradiction arm, so the only difference is that the stamps name no chain, and it freezes the blind reading that the drift had been producing by accident. The frozen set goes 20 -> 21 entries. ⚠ That count is cited in earlier tickets' conditions; it is moving here, on purpose, and this line is the notice.

4. The suite's own guard proves the addition was not smuggled: `no fixture was added without being frozen` FAILED when the scenario existed without its entry, and passes once the entry is present. A new fixture with no baseline is caught by the file itself.
5. verdict-logic.test.ts goes 28 tests: 26 passed, 2 failed -> 29 tests: 29 passed, 0 failed. THE SUITE IS FULLY GREEN FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE T8, and nothing in it was deleted to get there.

6. PRE-REGISTRATION, posted to the board at 12:3xZ BEFORE the candidate arm was taken: opens are exactly two, verdict-logic.test.ts and verdict-logic.frozen.json, and the frozen file GAINS one entry and needs no edit to the existing two. Both halves held. The board line also said that if the existing entries turned out to need editing, the correction was wrong and THAT was the finding - it did not.

7. OPENS DERIVED BY THE SWEEP, NOT WRITTEN: opens-sweep --compare out/t25-base-20261004T122912Z.tsv out/t25-cand-20261004T125143Z.tsv, two full declared-population arms at commit 1db1f1dc97c49a68a7c86d6a75187acae442788a (base dirty=no, candidate dirty=yes, same tool 439df9f31ecc): 100 of 103 comparable identical, 3 moved, 0 register-excluded, 4 printed no count line. DERIVED opens (2): src/mica/verdict-logic.frozen.json and src/mica/verdict-logic.test.ts, both 'edited, uncommitted'. src/core-door/core-door.test.ts and src/glue/glue.test.ts moved as the door objecting, and the comparison now NAMES THE CAUSE IT RECORDED - 'DOOR-DRIFT:src/mica/verdict-logic.frozen.json,src/mica/verdict-logic.test.ts' - which is exactly the two edited files. That caption is derived rather than guessed as of f71e685, and this is its first real derivation.

8. NO LIVE VERDICT MOVES. Checked on the record rather than argued: decision 615 reads MICA/Sig SILENT, and the live clerk stamps carry chain identity where these fixtures did not. readers.gate4Sunset remains undeclared and is not touched here.

9. ⚠ WHAT THIS TICKET DOES NOT FIX, so the grant is not read wider than it is: src/integration/l0-clerk-f3.test.ts fails from the SAME T8 cause at line 168 (asserts ALARM, reads CANNOT_ASSESS) and is NOT opened here. That suite forks a REAL clerkd and reads REAL receipts, so its stamps carry no chain identity because the clerk does not write one - which is a question about the clerk and the live stamps file, posted to section 1 at 12:0xZ and not mine to settle. It is also why that suite prints NO COUNT LINE: the assertion throws uncaught before any tally.

10. ⛔ AND THE STRUCTURAL FINDING THIS TICKET IS EVIDENCE FOR, recorded here because a ticket is where it will be read: T8 had the full ceremony - drafted, derived, signed, installed, re-pinned, spent - and its `opens` were the files it EDITED. Nothing in that ceremony asks which expectations elsewhere the new rule BLINDS, and the sweep cannot answer it either, because after the change the failure is a constant and a differential cannot see a constant. A ticket's conditions should name the suites its rule could blind, not only the files it edits.
